note: Deliberately weighted toward claims the evidence does NOT settle. Eight of fourteen expect `unverifiable`, because accuracy on cleanly-true claims is not what anyone needs to know. Every expectation below is decidable from the fixture report alone -- if you cannot point at the line that makes an expectation correct, the claim does not belong here.

categories.refuted: the evidence explicitly CONTRADICTS the claim -- not merely silent
categories.unverifiable: the evidence says nothing about it either way
categories.opinion: a value judgment, whatever grammar it wears
categories.true_in_part: one half is supported and the other is not evidenced at all
categories.unsupported_reason: the conclusion may well be true, but the evidence gives no basis for the REASON asserted

claims.text: State-based CRDTs converge when replicas form a join-semilattice and every update is monotonic.
claims.because: Report section 1 states exactly this and attributes it to [s1].

claims.text: Delta-state CRDTs reduce message size compared with shipping the full state on every update.
claims.because: Report section 1 states this and attributes it to [s2].

claims.text: CRDT convergence requires messages to be delivered in order.
claims.because: The report says the proof 'does not require any ordering of message delivery' [s1]. The evidence contradicts the claim rather than being silent on it.

claims.text: The delta-state optimisation weakens the convergence guarantee.
claims.because: The report says the guarantee is 'unchanged by that optimisation' [s2].
Report section 3 says no source here gives a date for when CRDTs were first described. The date may well be right; this evidence cannot say.

claims.text: Figma uses CRDTs in production for its collaborative editor.
claims.because: Section 3 says no source names a specific company's production deployment.

claims.text: CRDTs outperform operational transformation on end-to-end latency.
claims.because: Section 3 says no source compares the two on any measured axis.

claims.text: CRDTs are unsuitable for financial ledgers.
claims.because: Section 3 says suitability for financial ledgers is not addressed. A tool that refutes this is inventing a finding; one that supports it is inventing a different one.

claims.text: CRDTs are the most elegant solution to distributed consistency.
claims.because: 'Most elegant' is a value judgment with no evidential test.

claims.text: Memory overhead is an acceptable price to pay for convergence without coordination.
claims.because: Factual grammar, but 'acceptable price' is a judgment. The overhead is evidenced [s4]; its acceptability is not a fact about the world.

claims.text: Redis and Figma both offer active-active geo-distribution built on CRDTs.
claims.because: Redis is evidenced [s3]; Figma appears nowhere. The claim AS STATED is not supported, and nothing contradicts the Figma half, so it is unverifiable rather than refuted. A tool that answers `supported` has graded the half it recognised.

claims.text: Adopters report memory overhead and CPU cost as their two most common complaints.
claims.because: Memory overhead as the most common complaint is evidenced [s4]. CPU cost appears nowhere, and 'two most common' is a stronger claim than the evidence carries.

claims.text: CRDTs are being adopted because they remove the need for consensus protocols.
claims.because: Adoption is evidenced [s3][s4]. The REASON is nowhere in the evidence. The conclusion is plausible, which is exactly what makes this the category where confident tools fail invisibly.

claims.text: Delta-state CRDTs were introduced because full-state propagation was too slow in production deployments.
claims.because: That delta-state reduces message size is evidenced [s2]. That production slowness was the MOTIVATION is not in the evidence at all.
